extracted.intended_audience: authors of research software, prospective reviewers, and editors considering submissions to JOSS
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and criteria describing how JOSS handles submissions of research software and associated short papers, what reviewers evaluate, and how review is conducted and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review scope (paper + software)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every JOSS submission undergoes full external peer review, conducted by independent reviewers with relevant domain expertise. Both the paper and the software are reviewed: reviewers evaluate the quality, documentation, and design of the software as well as the accuracy and completeness of the paper itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews assess both software and paper together; see the separate reviewer guidelines and review criteria for full details. Reviewers should comment on software quality, documentation, design, and on the paper's accuracy and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open/public review record
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews take place openly via public GitHub issues in the JOSS reviews repository, meaning the full review record (all reviewer comments, author responses, and editorial decisions) is permanently and publicly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All review interactions, decisions, and production matters occur in public GitHub threads; authors and reviewers should expect transparency and permanence of the review record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection — independent domain expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is conducted by independent reviewers with relevant domain expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be externally independent and have domain-relevant expertise to judge both the software and the accompanying paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial role and expected review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors focus on ensuring reviews are thorough and that authors receive substantive, constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JOSS automates routine editorial tasks (PDF compilation, licence checking, DOI registration, Crossref deposit) so editors can prioritize the quality of reviews and constructive engagement with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a substantial scholarly contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS introduced clearer criteria for what constitutes a substantial scholarly contribution (2020) and updated criteria in 2026 to focus on human creativity, design thinking, and demonstrable research impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are evaluated for whether the software/paper represent a substantial scholarly contribution; as of 2026 emphasis is placed on human creativity, design thinking, and demonstrable research impact (in part as a response to generative AI tools). See the review criteria for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and publication model
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS is a diamond open access journal (free to read, free to publish) published by Open Journals with the aim of giving research software a citable, peer-reviewed home without article processing charges or subscription fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is free for authors and readers; operational transparency (cost model, analytics) is provided and the journal operates under the fiscal sponsorship of NumFOCUS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct (Code of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although spaces may feel informal at times, we want to remind authors and reviewers (and anyone else) that this is a professional space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants in submissions and reviews are expected to behave professionally; the Code of Conduct applies to authors, reviewers, and editors interacting in public review threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-specific submission restriction (LLM involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one listed editor explicitly states: 'NO LLM SUBMISSIONS. i will not participate in a submission that is written by, designed for, or involves LLMs in some major capacity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects an editor-level preference/restriction rather than necessarily a journal-wide ban; authors should note individual editors' stated boundaries when seeking handling editors or collaborators.
